correctness.rationale: The automorphism coordinates (A,f) have A in GL(V), f:V→Λ²V, and W-action Λ²A. The equation (A,f)^2=I gives A²=I and fA+(Λ²A)f=0. Since char q odd, V=U⊕T with eigensigns + and −, W+=Λ²U⊕Λ²T (dim a) and W−=U∧T (dim b). Thus f(U)⊆W−, f(T)⊆W+ and exactly q^(rb+ta) solutions per A. A central shear h=−(1/2)fA conjugates f to 0; quotient involutions with identical r are GL-conjugate. For the model (A,0), P centralizes A iff P preserves both eigenspaces; central g must obey gA=(Λ²A)g, so g(U)⊆W+,g(T)⊆W−; centralizer |GL_r||GL_t|q^(ra+tb). Independently orbit-stabilizer gives same class size using |Aut|=|GL_n|q^(n binom(n,2)). For r=0, I=q^(n binom(n,2)); Gaussian upper estimate [n choose r]_q<=K_q q^(rt) and exact exponent difference bound the total other classes by K_q q^(−n²/4)/(1−q^(−n²/4)) for n>=20. Independent exact integer tests for q=3,5,7 and n=3..35 verified orbit-centralizer identities and the n>=20 upper bound; the small n<20 were NEVER used to claim the asymptotic bound.
residual_risks: Odd characteristic essential (1/2 shear and semisimple involutions). n>=20 only for quantitative bound; base count valid n>=3. No classification in characteristic two or central quotients.

value.rationale: Conjugacy class multiplicities, centralizer sizes and an asymptotic dominant class form a complete natural structural profile of the unbounded free class-two nilpotent Lie algebra automorphism groups. The exterior-square eigenspace arithmetic makes the actual sizes far from a renaming of matrix involution counts, and the large-n concentration law is a useful qualitative transition. General linear-algebra tools are inputs but the exact closed census for the family is a motivated classification.
residual_risks: All odd finite field orders only, excludes proper quotients and characteristic two.

final_claim: For odd prime-power q and n>=3, Aut(V⊕Λ²V), with free bracket v∧w, has exactly one conjugacy class of involutions for each r=dim(+1 eigenspace of induced GL_n action), 0<=r<n; identity r=n. With t=n−r, a=binom(r,2)+binom(t,2), b=rt, centralizer |GL_r(q)||GL_t(q)|q^(ra+tb), class size [n choose r]_q q^(rt+rb+ta), and order-dividing-two automorphisms concentrate at r=0 as n grows (explicit n>=20 Gaussian-geometric bound).
limitations: The automorphism semidirect product is existing mathematics and must not be advertised as new.
Long-rank tail estimate n>=20 is sufficient, not optimal.
